title: ContextFact: Remembering Facts in Context for Long-Term Conversational Agents
title_zh: ContextFact：为长期对话智能体记住事实及其上下文
abstract_en: Agents built on large language models must maintain continuity across repeated interactions with users. However, long-term conversations scatter facts across turns and sessions, making it difficult to retrieve the right evidence with enough context. Memory for such conversations must therefore preserve facts with their context while keeping evidence selectively accessible. We first study how memory construction and retrieval-unit boundaries affect answerability and evidence access. Reading the entire memory bank reveals gaps that cannot be resolved by retrieval selection alone, showing that some context must be preserved during memory construction. Adjacent-turn grouping improves evidence access at matched unique-turn budgets, while wider windows do not consistently help. This motivates keeping fact-specific context local while organizing cross-session evidence separately. We propose ContextFact, which links context-preserving fact memories with source-grounded entity representations. Within sessions, it gathers the context needed to interpret each fact. Across sessions, it aligns recurring referents and revisits the source dialogue to reconstruct coherent entity representations linked to the supporting facts. At query time, ContextFact retrieves fact and entity views, reranks them independently, and uses entity-linked expansion to surface related facts; complete entity representations then provide organized cross-session evidence. With Qwen3.5-27B as the backbone, ContextFact achieves state-of-the-art performance while using only $21\%$ of the evidence tokens consumed by the strongest evaluated baseline, obtaining $86.49\%$ overall judge accuracy on LoCoMo and $91.00\%$ on LongMemEval-S. Controlled ablations support context-preserving fact boundaries and source-grounded entity reconstruction, while entity readout improves multi-hop accuracy beyond adding more facts.
abstract_zh: 长期对话中的事实分散在不同轮次和会话中，智能体既要保留理解事实所需的上下文，又要能按需检索证据。研究发现，即使读取整个记忆库，部分问题仍无法回答，说明仅改进检索无法弥补记忆构建时丢失的上下文。在覆盖的不同对话轮次数相同的条件下，将相邻轮次分组能改善证据获取，但扩大窗口并不总是有益。为此，ContextFact 在会话内为每条事实保留必要的上下文，在会话间对齐反复出现的指称对象，并回溯原始对话，重建与支持事实相链接的实体表示。查询时，系统分别检索并重排序事实和实体，再沿实体链接补充相关事实，并用完整的实体表示组织跨会话证据。以 Qwen3.5-27B 为骨干模型，ContextFact 在 LoCoMo 和 LongMemEval-S 上的总体评判准确率分别达到 86.49% 和 91.00%，取得最先进水平，且证据 token 用量仅为参评最强基线的 21%。消融实验验证了保留事实语境和基于原始对话重建实体的价值；在多跳问答中，读取实体表示比单纯增加事实更有效。
key_points_zh: 即使读取完整记忆库，部分问题仍不可回答：构建记忆时丢失的语境，无法仅靠改进检索补回。
在覆盖的不同对话轮次数相同的条件下，相邻轮次分组有助于获取证据，但更宽的窗口并不总是更好。
ContextFact 在会话内保留事实语境，在会话间基于原始对话重建实体；查询时分别重排序事实和实体，并沿实体链接扩展证据。
以 Qwen3.5-27B 为骨干，LoCoMo 和 LongMemEval-S 的总体评判准确率分别为 86.49% 和 91.00%，证据 token 用量仅为参评最强基线的 21%。
消融实验显示，在多跳问答中，读取完整实体表示比单纯增加事实更能提高准确率。

agent-memory.reason: 核心贡献是面向长期文本对话代理的外部记忆：将事实与理解所需的上下文一起存储，并回查原始对话重建跨会话实体，支持关联检索。两个基准量化了准确率与证据开销；固定预算对照和消融表明，保留完整事实优于拆分，直接提供实体表征比单纯增加事实更有利于多跳问答。
